title: Qubic Secures CA$1.5 Million ($1.08 Million USD) Canadian Federal Contract for Cryogenic Amplifiers - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Sherbrooke-based Qubic won a Canadian federal contract worth up to CA$1.5M (US$1.08M) through Innovative Solutions Canada to deliver nine kinetic inductance traveling wave parametric amplifiers plus software from late 2026 through spring 2027. Its KI-TWPAs dissipate under 0.1 mW versus conventional cryogenic amplifiers that consume up to 50% of a dilution refrigerator's cooling power, and avoid magnetic-field-sensitive Josephson junctions; the award follows a CA$3.5M seed led by Two Small Fish Ventures and brings total raised to nearly CA$10M.

insights.claim: Cryogenic signal-processing developer Qubic signed a contract with an agency of the Canadian federal government valued at up to CA$1.5 million (US$1.08 million), awarded through the Innovative Solutions Canada Testing Stream.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small in absolute terms but it is government validation revenue — the reference customer that unlocks larger procurement for component suppliers.
insights.locator: Cryogenic signal-processing developer Qubic has signed

insights.claim: Qubic will deliver nine Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifiers with mounting accessories and evaluation software starting in late 2026, with final evaluation milestones scheduled through spring 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Nine units implies roughly CA$167k per amplifier-plus-software bundle, a useful benchmark for pricing cryogenic readout components.
insights.locator: Under the contract terms, Sherbrooke-based Qubic will deliver

insights.claim: The procurement is explicitly focused on de-risking the RF sensor supply chain through real-world federal agency testing rather than pure research.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Governments treating quantum components as a supply-chain security issue means more sovereign-sourcing contracts for domestic vendors.
insights.locator: Focus: De-risking RF Sensor Supply Chain

themes.theme: Thermal budget as the scaling constraint

insights.claim: Conventional cryogenic amplifiers consume up to 50% of a dilution refrigerator's available cooling power, whereas Qubic's hardware reduces thermal dissipation to under 0.1 mW per device.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Freeing half a fridge's cooling budget directly increases how many qubits fit per refrigerator — a hard economic lever on scaling cost per qubit.
insights.quote: Unlike conventional cryogenic amplifiers that consume up to 50% of a dilution refrigerator’s available cooling power, Qubic’s hardware reduces thermal dissipation to under 0.1 mW.

insights.claim: Qubic's KI-TWPA architecture draws its non-linear inductance directly from the superconducting transmission line material instead of relying on magnetic-field-sensitive Josephson junctions, producing a magnetic-field-resilient device operating near the quantum limit.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Field resilience opens applications beyond qubit readout into magnetic-field environments like RF sensing and dark-matter/defense instrumentation.
insights.locator: Rather than relying on magnetic-field-sensitive Josephson junctions

insights.claim: The amplifiers are designed to support multiplexed qubit readout and high-sensitivity RF sensing, giving the same component two distinct end markets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Dual-use components have a shorter path to revenue than quantum-computing-only parts, since sensing budgets exist today.
insights.locator: operates near the quantum limit to support multiplexed qubit readout

insights.claim: The federal award brings Qubic's total raised capital and non-dilutive grant funding to nearly CA$10 million, following a CA$3.5 million (US$2.5 million) seed round led by Two Small Fish Ventures in June 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A heavy non-dilutive mix means founders retain more equity and the company can survive long qualification cycles typical of cryogenic hardware.
insights.locator: The federal procurement follows commercial momentum

insights.claim: Qubic is a spin-off from the Institut Quantique and the Institute for Quantum Computing, placing it directly in Canada's established academic quantum cluster.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Canadian university spinouts remain a reliable deal-flow channel for quantum components; academic pedigree correlates with federal contract access.
insights.locator: the spin-off from the Institut Quantique

insights.claim: Qubic has executed a commercial integration partnership with quantum control developer Quantum Machines to incorporate its low-noise KI-TWPAs into hybrid control stacks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Embedding into an established control-stack vendor is the distribution route that turns a component startup into a volume supplier.
insights.locator: as well as a commercial integration partnership executed
